12a_1_pair_curvatures.png: The curvature of the corrected metric at the sample point $H = 1$, $a_4' = 0.6$, $a_4^{\prime\prime} = 0.3$, $u = 0.8$, $v = 0.1$, $k = 1.5$, in units of $H^2$. Left: the 8 by 8 table of the sectional curvatures $K_{ab}$ of the planes of $x_a$ and $x_b$, with the value in each cell; the five groups of values are visible as blocks. Right: the 28 by 28 table of all components $R^{ab}{}_{mn}$ with $a < b$, $m < n$ (rows the upper pairs, columns the lower pairs); only the diagonal is coloured, because the corrected metric has no mixed curvature component. Red positive, blue negative, white zero.
12a_2_einstein_components.png: The three distinct components of the Einstein tensor of the corrected metric along the record history $a_4 = Hx_4$, $b_4 = e^{(4/3)Hx_4}$, as functions of the time $x_4$ (units $1/H$), in units of $H^2$: the time component $G^{x_4}{}_{x_4} = (18k + 1)/3$ (solid), the 3-space component $G^{x_1}{}_{x_1} = (54k - 13)/9$ (dashed) and the common component of the hidden direction and the extra times $G^{x_0}{}_{x_0} = (9k - 11)/3$ (dotted), with $k = e^{2a_4}/b_4 = e^{(2/3)Hx_4}$. All three grow with $k$, the curvature of the shrinking block; the 3-space and block components differ, so a source of this history cannot have equal pressures.
12a_3_lovelock_heat_maps.png: The three Lovelock tensors $E_{(1)}$ (the Einstein tensor), $E_{(2)}$ (the Gauss-Bonnet tensor) and $E_{(3)}$ of the corrected metric as 8 by 8 tables, row $h$ and column $j$ running over $x_0$ to $x_7$, evaluated at $H = 1$, $a_4' = 0.6$, $a_4^{\prime\prime} = 0.3$, $u = 0.8$, $v = 0.1$, $k = 1.5$; the colour is the value (each panel with its own scale, red positive, blue negative, white zero) and the number in each diagonal cell is the value. All off-diagonal entries are zero, and each tensor has only three different diagonal values: one for 3-space, one for the time, and one for the hidden direction and the three extra times together.
12a_4_jacobian_determinant.png: The determinant of the Jacobian $J$ with which $a_4^{\prime\prime}$ and $v = (b_4'/b_4)'$ enter the 3-space and hidden equations, along the record history $a_4 = Hx_4$, $b_4 = e^{(4/3)Hx_4}$, as a function of the time $x_4$ (units $1/H$, $H = 1$): Einstein gravity ($-3$, solid), Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity with $\alpha_2H^2 = 0.01$ (dashed) and $1/32$ (dash-dotted), and the author's weights (dotted). All four stay below zero, so along this history the two equations of second order can always be solved for $a_4^{\prime\prime}$ and $v$; where $\det J$ vanished they could not.
12a_5_exponential_vacuum.png: Why no exponential history $a_4 = AHx_4 + a_0$, $b_4 = b_4(0)e^{\beta AHx_4}$ solves the vacuum equations of Einstein gravity: in the plane of $\beta$ (horizontal) and $k/A^2$ (vertical, $k = e^{2a_4}/b_4$), the 3-space equation minus the time equation holds only on the dashed lines $\beta = 2$ and $\beta = 4$, the hidden equation minus the time equation only on the solid line $k/A^2 = (\beta - 4)/2$. The two meet at the black points $(2, -1)$ and $(4, 0)$, both in the grey region $k \leq 0$, where no history lies. The dotted line is the record history $\beta = 4/3$.
